limit: The explicit source_instance and tenant_scope bind only the Manifest root; no vehicle or trailer provider ID path, wire type, uniqueness, immutability or stability contract exists.
counterexample: A plate signal can repeat for distinct unidentified vehicles or move between them without a provider identity.

limit: Plate is preserved only as bounded Manifest observation text; no versioned normalizer, validator, collision, reuse, reassignment or rekey policy exists.
counterexample: The same textual plate may denote distinct vehicles across time and roles.

limit: Carrier nickname is Manifest context only; it is not a stable vehicle owner, assignment, source or tenant key.
counterexample: A Manifest branch can differ from the vehicle owner or current assignment branch.

limit: Manifest freshness, replay and absence rules do not define effective intervals, current/history, entity absence, vehicle-level conflict or rekey.
counterexample: Two Manifest observations can be ordered without defining which vehicle master version is current.

limit: Distinct paths prove observation roles only; they do not prove dimensional identities, cross-Manifest stability or position-change semantics.
counterexample: Collapsing equal plate text across main, trailer 1 and trailer 2 would erase role provenance.

limit: The explicit source_instance and tenant_scope bind only the Manifest root; no driver provider ID path, wire type, uniqueness, immutability or stability contract exists.
counterexample: The same name can denote distinct people while a renamed person can have different names.

limit: The legacy normalized-name grouping and generic substring exclusion are counterevidence, not an identity or lifecycle contract.
counterexample: Homonyms merge while rename, merge and split events fragment or repoint a person without an immutable ID.

limit: Driver contract type is only contextual text in a Manifest; no ontology, parties, effective interval or change semantics are versioned.
counterexample: A contextual label cannot prove a person, employment relationship or its validity.

limit: Carrier nickname is Manifest context only; it is not a stable driver assignment, source or tenant key.
counterexample: A driver can operate a Manifest from a branch different from a formal assignment branch.

limit: Manifest freshness, replay and absence rules do not define effective intervals, current/history, entity absence, driver-level conflict or rekey.
counterexample: Two Manifest observations can be ordered without deciding rename, merge, split or the current driver master version.

limit: Cooccurrence belongs to one Manifest observation and does not prove a stable relationship, join key or cardinality.
counterexample: The same cooccurring signals can be temporary and cannot create a canonical foreign key.
